# Morandi — OCV reconfiguration against the 2016-08 … 2017-07 reference, month by month

*generated by `code/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.py`; the metric is the pre-registered one of `code/sds/ocv_reconfigure_spec.md` (behaviour block, log transform, reference MAD), read here as a monthly series. It is not a new test, and it carries none.*

Ponte Morandi (Polcevera), Genova: one support-sized chip per acquisition (51 x 137 cells, 861 support cells, 30 m guard, 200 m ring), 207 acquisitions in two tracks (94 A_asc, 113 A_des). The record splits, by its own state column, into a **reference** of 99 chips (2016-08-24 … 2017-07-28), the **series** of 99 chips on 13 months (2017-08 … 2018-08), and 9 post-collapse chips that are counted and never plotted.

```
z(month) = ( median(log x_month) - median(log x_ref) ) / MAD(log x_ref)
x        = gamma2, P            both on the log scale
R        = rms over the two dimensions (gamma2, P)
ref      = 2016-08-24 .. 2017-07-28   n = 99 chips on 12 months
series   = 2017-08-01 .. 2018-08-08   99 chips on 13 months, 3-11 per month
```

The reference is drawn from the twelve months *before* the series, so the origin of everything below is the bridge's own earlier state and not a baseline chosen after the fact. `0` on both axes is that state; it is not a norm and not a threshold.

**The unit is the support-sized chip, not the paper figure's export.** This table has 207 rows on 51 x 137 chips; `fig_morandi_ocv_paper` reads the 232-row per-track export. The two are not mixed, and the γ² levels are not comparable between them — only z, which is in each figure's own reference MADs.

## Why this window

The record starts 2016-08-24; the series is the last twelve months before the collapse, so the reference can only be built from what precedes 2017-08. Four windows were available, and the choice is stated rather than buried because it moves the answer:

| window | chips | months | ASC / DESC | contains the series? | used | why |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2016-08-01 … 2016-12-31 | 36 | 5 | 18 / 18 | no | — | too short: five months, one season, and it throws away the rest of the only full year the record holds |
| 2016-08-01 … 2017-07-31 | 99 | 12 | 53 / 46 | no | **used** | used: twelve months, every calendar month once, and the series is held out entirely |
| 2016-08-01 … 2017-12-31 | 147 | 17 | 75 / 72 | yes | — | already contains the first five series months, so the series would help set its own origin |
| 2016-08-01 … 2018-08-13 | 198 | 25 | 91 / 107 | yes | — | the SDS plate's whole pre-collapse reference: it contains all thirteen series months |

Only the used window is a full year *and* earlier than the series. A per-calendar-month baseline is not on the list because a single month of the reference holds 5-10 chips, below `SCALE_MIN_REF = 10`: such a baseline has no MAD. That limit is stated rather than engineered around.

## The reference

| dim | column | n | median | MAD(log) | 1 MAD = factor | scale used |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| gamma2 | `gamma2_mask` | 99 | 0.04538 | 1.0173 | 2.766 | mad |
| P | `P` | 99 | 0.09517 | 0.5309 | 1.701 | mad |

Both scales are the reference's own MAD: n = 99 is far above `SCALE_MIN_REF = 10` for both dimensions, so the fallback chain is not used. The reference has no missing month between 2016-08 and 2017-07, and its track mix is 53 A_asc / 46 A_des (ASC share 0.54).

`n` is the number of chips the month's median rests on, `✱` marks a month below `SMALL_N = 6` — here 1 of 13, 2018-08 — and `–` would be a cell the record does not contain, never a zero. The interval is the *reference's* uncertainty: 2000 circular moving-block draws of the 99 reference chips with the reference median **and** scale re-estimated inside each draw, the month's chips held fixed. It answers "how well is the origin known", not "how well is the month known".

## The two tracks

The two Sentinel-1 geometries are not interchangeable: their reference medians differ by 8.5x in γ² and 2.8x in P, and the mix moves from 53/46 to 38/61. A pooled median therefore moves when *which track is sampled* changes, even if neither track moves. The split below is the control: each track's monthly median against **its own** reference median, shown twice — in that track's own MAD (`z own`) and in the **pooled** reference MAD (`z pooled`, the unit of the month table and of panels a/b). The second is the one the figure draws; it is comparable to the headline, while `z own` answers whether the track moved in its own units.

| track | n_ref | gamma2 median | gamma2 MAD(log) | P median | P MAD(log) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A_asc (ASC) | 53 | 0.08778 | 0.4633 | 0.1591 | 0.2292 |
| A_des (DESC) | 46 | 0.01038 | 1.4136 | 0.05698 | 0.1941 |

The two tracks' own MADs differ by a factor 3.1 in γ². Re-referencing each to its own MAD would therefore move a month by several MADs for the level offset alone, which is why the figure uses the pooled unit. The split is a composition control, not a second estimate.

## The mix

What the pooled median would do if each track stayed at its own reference median and only the ASC/DESC counts changed. It is a linear reconstruction of the composition effect, and because the median is an order statistic of a two-mode mixture, the realised effect can be larger:

| month | ASC / DESC | ASC share | mix-only Δz(gamma2) | mix-only Δz(P) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2017-08 | 5 / 6 | 0.45 | -0.17 | -0.16 |
| 2017-09 | 5 / 5 | 0.50 | -0.07 | -0.07 |
| 2017-10 | 5 / 5 | 0.50 | -0.07 | -0.07 |
| 2017-11 | 4 / 5 | 0.44 | -0.19 | -0.18 |
| 2017-12 | 3 / 5 | 0.38 | -0.34 | -0.31 |
| 2018-01 | 2 / 5 | 0.29 | -0.52 | -0.48 |
| 2018-02 | 2 / 5 | 0.29 | -0.52 | -0.48 |
| 2018-03 | 3 / 5 | 0.38 | -0.34 | -0.31 |
| 2018-04 | 2 / 4 | 0.33 | -0.42 | -0.39 |
| 2018-05 | 2 / 5 | 0.29 | -0.52 | -0.48 |
| 2018-06 | 2 / 4 | 0.33 | -0.42 | -0.39 |
| 2018-07 | 2 / 5 | 0.29 | -0.52 | -0.48 |
| 2018-08 | 1 / 2 | 0.33 | -0.42 | -0.39 |

The largest linear mix-only change is 0.52 MAD for γ² and 0.48 for P. The γ² path reaches -3.22 MAD, so the mix alone does not explain it; the within-track tables above show where the rest comes from. The mix-only column is a lower bound, not a correction.

## What the series shows

**The pooled γ² is below the reference in every month; P is not.** The median z(gamma2) runs -0.55 (2017-10) to -3.22 (2018-03), negative in 13 of 13 months; 6 gamma2 month(s) (2017-12, 2018-01, 2018-02, 2018-03, 2018-04, 2018-08) lie beyond ±2 MAD. z(P) runs -0.84 (2018-08) to +0.59 (2018-04), is positive in 7 of 13 months and never reaches ±2. The largest |z| anywhere is 3.22. On the pooled number alone the bridge reads as less echo-consistent and no less persistent than in 2016-08 … 2017-07. The largest two-month change is -2.00 of gamma2 between 2017-10 and 2017-12 (-0.55 -> -2.56); the path is not monotone.

**The γ² drop is not shared by the two tracks, and the pooled median is not their average.** Against its own reference, A_asc's γ² stays within ±1.7 in 10 of 13 months; the 3 exceptions (2018-04, 2018-05, 2018-08) are all months with n ≤ 2. A_des's γ² is below its own reference in 13 of 13 months (-2.56 to -0.34 of its own MAD). So one track moves and the other does not. The pooled median is an order statistic of a two-mode mixture whose modes are 8.5x apart (0.08778 vs 0.01038): when ASC holds fewer than half the chips, the median is a DESC value and can sit below *both* track medians (2018-03: pooled -3.22, ASC +0.09, DESC -2.76 in pooled-MAD units). The pooled excursion is therefore a mixture of a real DESC drop, the track level offset and the order statistic — not a whole-deck signal.

**P rises inside both tracks and the mix cancels it.** A_asc's P is above its own reference in 11 of 13 months (own-MAD z up to +1.96; pooled unit at most +0.85), A_des's in 13 of 13 (own-MAD up to +2.37; pooled at most +0.86), yet the pooled z(P) changes sign. The reason is the mix: A_des has the lower P level (0.057 vs 0.159) and gains 15 chips in the series. A linear mix-only reconstruction — both tracks held at their own reference medians, only the counts changed — gives -0.52 to -0.07 MAD for γ² and -0.48 to -0.07 for P. Because the median is an order statistic, that linear number is a *lower bound*, not the whole composition effect.

**The composition moves in one direction, and the series is thin where it matters.** The reference is 53 ASC / 46 DESC (ASC share 0.54); the series is 38 / 61 (0.38). Per month the ASC count falls from 5 of 11 to 1 of 3 while DESC stays at 4–6. The last month, 2018-08, holds 3 chips (2018-08-02, 2018-08-04, 2018-08-08; 1 ASC + 2 DESC) and is the only month below `SMALL_N = 6`. Its marker is z(gamma2) = -2.43 [-3.57, -1.57], z(P) = -0.84 [-1.36, -0.34], R = 1.82. The interval is narrow because the *origin* is well known, not because the month is: with three chips the month's own sampling noise is not bounded by anything this figure computes.

**R stays inside the reference's own 5–95 % band except one low.** The band is 0.49–3.11; R runs 0.46 to 2.28. It never reaches the 95th percentile, and only 2017-10 falls below the 5th (0.46, n = 10). A low R is *agreement* with the origin on both dimensions, so it is not a departure; a high R would be, and none reaches the band's upper edge.

**The pooled-window sensitivity shows how much of the number is the origin.** Re-centring on the 198-chip pre-collapse record instead of the 99-chip reference (γ² MAD 1.02 -> 1.68) compresses z(γ²) to -1.47 … +0.14 and z(P) to -0.90 … +0.68. That pool contains the series, so it is a declared sensitivity to the window — not validation, and not a second estimate.

**One sentence.** Between 2017-08-01 and 2018-08-08 the pooled chip sits below its 2016-08 … 2017-07 γ² level and on its P level, but the split shows that this is a low-γ² DESC track entering a larger share of the pool, not a bridge-wide reconfiguration; on this record the honest reading is a null.

## What it does not say

* **The binding limit is sampling, not SNR.** A month rests on 3-11 chips (1-5 ASC, 2-6 DESC), so 2018-08 alone is `thin` (`n = 3 < SMALL_N = 6`) and its "median" *is* the middle of three chips. Every other month is 6–11 acquisitions, enough for a median and not enough for a spread: the monthly marker is the median of the chips that exist, not of the month, and a month with no acquisition would be a gap, not a value.
* **The interval belongs to the reference.** It says how well a 99-chip origin is known under a resampling of those chips. It is not a confidence interval for a monthly value: the month's own sampling noise is not in it. That is why the n = 3 month's interval is narrow for the wrong reason.
* **This `gamma2_mask` is not the `gamma2` of the paper figure.** The support-sized chip is 51 x 137 cells with 861 support cells (30 m guard, 200 m ring), and its reference median `gamma2_mask` is 0.04538. The echo-mask γ² of `fig_morandi_ocv_paper` is computed on the full 80 x 80 chip of the 232-chip export and runs several times higher. Only the *standardised* quantity z is comparable between the two figures; the levels are not, and neither is R.
* **The chip is a support rectangle, not a damage map.** The 207-row table is the ring-supported chip; it is a window on the deck, not a map of the failure. Nothing here localises damage, and the plate makes no claim about the 2018-08-14 collapse; it describes how the chip's echo behaviour moved while the bridge stood. The paper figure's structural caveat — its analysed window is not on the collapsed span — is the frame this chip sits in, and nothing here changes it.
* **The series stops at the collapse, deliberately.** The 9 acquisitions after 2018-08-14 (2018-08-14 … 2018-09-13) are the same bridge in a different state, and they are counted in the audit and carry no value here. The record does not end at the event; the *series* does.
* **The reference window is a choice, and it moves the answer.** The first twelve months give a full seasonal cycle and are strictly earlier than the series. The alternatives are in the candidate table: five months are too few; the 17- and 25-month windows *contain* the series. The 99-chip reference is the only candidate that is both long enough to have a MAD and held out before the months it standardises.
* **The pooled sensitivity is not a second estimate.** Re-centring on the 198-chip pre-collapse record changes the γ² MAD from 1.02 to 1.68 and the P MAD from 0.53 to 0.48; it contains the series, so it is a declared sensitivity to the window chosen above, not independent evidence.
* **The track split is a composition control, not two estimates.** The two tracks' reference γ² MADs are 0.463 (A_asc) and 1.414 (A_des), and their levels differ by 8.5x. Re-referencing each to its own MAD would move a month by the level offset alone — 1.5 DESC MADs and 4.6 ASC MADs — before any change, so the figure standardises the within-track difference by the *pooled* MAD instead. The dotted lines therefore show direction, not effect size; with 1–5 ASC chips a month, the ASC line is itself a median of very few values and its n ≤ 2 excursions are the least stable points on the plate.
* **No test, no dose, no partner.** The sds H1/H2 machinery needs at least two states per block and, for a dose, an ordered ladder; here one state is sampled monthly. So there is no p-value, no Holm family and no cosine, ±2 MAD is a descriptive band and not a significance threshold, and these magnitudes are in this reference's own units — they are not comparable to the Carola or CTS reconfiguration amplitudes, whose records, chips and references are different.
* **The honest null stands.** `fig_morandi_ocv_paper.md` reports no detectable pre-collapse change on the 232-chip export; this plate does not overturn it. The pooled γ² offset is real *in the sample*, but the split attributes it to one track and a shifting mix rather than to a bridge-wide reconfiguration. No precursor, no damage and no reconfiguration claim is made; the monthly path is a description with n = 3–11 behind each point.

## Reproduce

```
python3 code/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.py            # data + figure
python3 code/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.py --selftest
python3 code/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.py --verify
bash figures/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.sh
```

The run reads `data/morandi/support/morandi_ocv_channels.csv` (sha256 `249c9ee6630c21df…`) and `data/morandi/support/morandi_ocv_channels_meta.json`, and writes `data/morandi/ocv_reconfiguration_morandi.json`, `data/morandi/ocv_reconfiguration_morandi_table.csv`, `figures/morandi/fig_morandi_ocv_reconfiguration.jpg` and this file. No timestamp enters either output, so a second run is byte-identical. `--selftest` re-derives the plate's invariants from the table; `--verify` recomputes the report and diffs it against the committed JSON (floats to 1e-9) before checking the CSV against the same object.

## The figure

* **(a)** z(gamma2) by month: one dot per chip (light), the month's median (filled), the reference's ±2 MAD band (grey), the 95 % reference-uncertainty bar, the chip-count strip at the bottom — split into A_asc and A_des, so the mix is visible under the points — and the collapse of 2018-08-14 as the red cut. The two dotted lines are the same months under the A_asc-only and A_des-only references, in pooled MAD units (the table in *The two tracks* is their source). The 2018-08 marker is ringed: n = 3.
* **(b)** z(P) on the same axis and the same reference — the two panels are read together, never as two independent verdicts.
* **(c)** the plane: the origin is the reference state, the grey cloud is the 99 reference chips, the path runs 2017-08 -> 2018-08 and is coloured by year-quarter (the series crosses 2017 and 2018), the thin arrows are the quarter medians, and the terminal month is ringed. The path is the pooled month; the cloud is the reference only.
* **(d)** R = rms(z gamma2, z P) per month against the empirical 5-95 % band of the reference chips' own R. A point below the band is *agreement* with the origin, not a departure.

The plate is 2 x 2 at 13.0 in and 600 dpi, the sds package's `savefig.dpi`; every number in it is read from the JSON this run writes.
